results.title: Cold Open
results.vo_quote: I didn't eat lunch today. My mom said I shouldn't.
results.description: Pure black screen. A child's voice speaks into the dark — present tense, quiet, real. The first sound of the film is a kid telling us he hasn't eaten today.

results.title: Wide Establishing — The Village
results.vo_quote: A few years ago, on a cold night in Ogden, a man walked up to the Giving Machines.
results.description: Wide cinematic establishing shot of the Ogden Christmas Village at night. Beautiful watercolor world — wet cobblestones, decorated trees, lampposts with golden halos, distant warmly-lit shops, dense painterly snow. No main characters yet. We're being shown where the legend begins.

results.title: Doug at the Machines
results.description: Doug — the volunteer — stands beside the three Giving Machines, hands in his coat pockets, waiting. The picture of a regular kind man doing a regular kind thing on a cold night. Unaware he's about to witness something he'll talk about for the rest of his life.

results.title: The Approach
results.vo_quote: He didn't look like he had much. But he had walked a long way to get there.
results.description: A man walks slowly toward the machines through the falling snow. Worn coat. Beanie. He doesn't look like the typical Giving Machines donor — and that's the whole point. We don't know yet what he's about to do.

results.title: Two-Shot at the Machine
results.vo_quote: This one feeds a kid for a week. Ten dollars buys a child their school lunch.
results.description: Doug shows the man the donation options — including the school lunch one. The machines glow between them. This is the moment a stranger learns what ten dollars can do.

results.title: The Recognition
results.vo_quote: Someone did that for me when I was a kid.
results.description: Extreme close-up on the man's face. Something has just landed inside him. Nothing dramatic — just a small change behind the eyes. We don't know yet what he's remembering. We only know he's somewhere else for a moment.

results.title: He Walks Away
results.description: The man turns and walks away into the village. Doug is left behind. We don't know yet if the story is over or just starting.

results.title: Boots in the Snow
results.description: Tight on a pair of worn boots crunching through fresh snow. He came back. We don't know what he came back with.

results.title: The Bill
results.vo_quote: I want to buy the lunches. Will you take cash?
results.description: The man's hand extending a folded $20 bill. Worn, creased, real. The only thing in sharp focus.

results.title: Doug's Reaction
results.vo_quote: I'm sorry — I don't have change for a twenty.
results.description: Doug's face as he understands what's happening. The bill he's been handed is not the donation. It's everything this man has.

results.title: The Pause
results.description: A beat. Two men looking at each other. The man considering. Doug waiting. The audience leaning forward.

results.title: Let's Get Two
results.vo_quote: Let's get two, then. Somebody did this for me.
results.description: The man with the smallest, gentlest smile. Saying the line that the entire film is named for. Calm, certain, dignified.

results.title: Walking Into the Light
results.vo_quote: He walked back into the night, and we never knew his name.
results.description: The man walks away into the village. Smaller and smaller. Becomes part of the lights. We will not see him again. The story he started is about to belong to someone else.

results.title: Transition — From Then to Now
results.vo_quote: His story is the reason we tell this one.
results.description: The warm yellow lamplight of the village dissolves into the warm yellow morning sun of a Davis County school cafeteria. Same color, different decade. Same story, different child.

results.title: Mateo at the Table
results.vo_quote: This is Mateo. He's eight. He's in a Davis County classroom right now.
results.description: A modern Davis County school cafeteria. Bright, sunlit, warm. Other kids eating, laughing quietly. One boy sits alone at the end of a table. Backpack still on. Empty space in front of him where a tray should be. He's not unhappy — he's careful. Like he's been told what to do and he's doing it.

results.title: The Empty Space
results.vo_quote: Mateo's family is behind on lunch payments. They want to stay invisible. So Mateo goes to school, and he doesn't eat.
results.description: Tight on the table in front of Mateo. No tray. No food. His small hands folded. The shot we feel in our chest before we hear the line that explains it.

results.title: The Other Kids
results.vo_quote: He's not the only one. In Davis County, one in seven kids carries an unpaid lunch balance.
results.description: A wider shot of the cafeteria. Other children — also real-proportioned, also cartoon-faced — eating, talking, normal. Mateo small in the frame, alone, the only still figure.

results.title: The Numbers
results.vo_quote: $10 buys one week of school lunch. $40 buys a month. $360 buys a child a year of meals they would not otherwise eat.
results.description: Cream watercolor background. Numbers appear in elegant red serif typography. The math of the problem.

results.title: The Tray Arrives
results.vo_quote: Lunch Angels are the people who quietly cover what a child can't.
results.description: A lunch tray slides quietly onto the table in front of Mateo. We don't see who placed it there. He looks up — surprise, then carefully concealed relief. Nobody made a fuss. Nobody said his name. He just gets to eat.

results.title: Mateo Eats
results.vo_quote: No one called his parents. No one said his name. He just got to eat.
results.description: Mateo, mid-bite. Eyes closed slightly. The relief of a kid who hasn't eaten all day finally eating. No drama. Just lunch.

results.title: The Wide Pull-Back
results.vo_quote: There are kids in our schools right now who aren't eating. Not because food isn't there. Because shame is.
results.description: Camera pulls back. Mateo eating becomes one figure in a wide cafeteria full of other kids — some of whom are also Mateos we never met. The film opens out into the bigger picture.

results.title: Be the Someone
results.description: End card. Cream watercolor background. The single line the entire film has been building toward, in deep red elegant serif. Below it: the URL where viewers go to give.
